top_stories.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Faces Board Investigation Over Alleged Chinese Intelligence Ties
points: Huang admitted Sunday to an affair with Alice Huang (also known as Huang Le), a Megaspeed executive identified by U.S. officials as connected to Chinese intelligence.

Megaspeed, a Singapore-based computer facility operator, purchased over $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips across two years; Nvidia kept selling to them even after a Commerce Department investigation began.

Nvidia's board formed an independent director committee with outside counsel to investigate potential security and governance risks, including classified-information access and conflict-of-interest concerns.

Huang remains CEO during the probe; no wrongdoing has been confirmed, and he's seen as unlikely to fully depart, though a shift to executive chairman (a senior role retaining strategic influence without day-to-day CEO duties) is possible given investor and political support.
Donald Trump called Huang a "fine person" and said he should remain CEO.

Nvidia shares fell in premarket/Friday trading on the news, while the broader Nasdaq and S&P 500 futures still advanced, suggesting markets are compartmentalizing the risk rather than broadly selling off tech.
The episode adds scrutiny to semiconductor industry security practices and export-control enforcement amid U.S.-China tensions, with possible implications for Nvidia's government contracts.

unique_angles.point: Investigation timing coincides with critical earnings season, creating added distraction and uncertainty for stakeholders; outcome could also trigger broader reviews of security clearances across defense contractors and chip makers.
Chip stocks broadly closed Friday nearly 20% below their 50-day moving average, reflecting sector-wide repricing of AI spending growth expectations alongside the Huang news.
The scandal lands right after the S&P 500's worst week since April 2025, and comes as Democrats' midterm landslide has investors betting on cooling AI spending and a Treasuries boost.

top_stories.title: Leaked Data Shows ~400,000 Russian Deaths in Ukraine War
points: Hacked confidential data, reportedly from Russia's state statistics agency Rosstat, points to approximately 400,000 deaths among Russian forces since the full-scale invasion began nearly five years ago.
Vladimir Putin has gone to great lengths to conceal the true scale of military losses, making this leak a rare public accounting of the war's human cost.

unique_angles.point: Some observers in Ukraine worry a Trump administration weakened by the midterms could prove an even less reliable partner going forward.

top_stories.title: October Jobs Report Beats Forecasts, Reviving December Rate-Hike Debate
points: U.S. economy added 165,000 jobs in October, more than double economist forecasts; September's figure was also revised up from 29,000 to 60,000.

Stronger-than-expected jobs data eases recession fears but raises inflation concerns, pushing up odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike (an increase in the central bank's benchmark interest rate) in December.
Prediction market Polymarket now prices a 78% probability of a quarter-point rate hike at the December Fed meeting.
Fed officials, including Mary Daly, have signaled additional rate increases may be needed despite earlier expectations of a prolonged pause.

unique_angles.point: This week's CPI (Tuesday, expected 0.2% month-over-month) and PPI (Friday, expected 0.4%) data will be key; Apollo strategist Torsten Slok argues rates may need to reach as high as 6.75% to hit the Fed's 2% inflation target, and a wave of Fed speakers (Goolsbee, Bowman, Waller, Barr, Barkin, Logan, Williams, Jefferson) will be watched closely since Fed Chair Warsh has avoided forward guidance.

top_stories.title: Stock Futures Point to Rebound After Worst Week Since April 2025
points: U.S. stock futures rose Monday as markets attempted to recover from the prior week's steep losses (S&P 500's worst week since April 2025).
S&P 500 futures were up about 0.5% and Nasdaq 100 futures up about 0.2%, even as Nvidia shares fell on the Huang investigation news.

unique_angles.point: The volatility is prompting some investors to reconsider cash strategies beyond traditional 5% CDs (certificates of deposit, a type of bank savings product with a fixed interest rate).

points: Agility Robotics (ticker AGLT) began trading, joining recent market momentum in the humanoid robot sector.

items.title: CoreWeave Eyes Texas Data Center Expansion
points: Cloud/AI infrastructure firm CoreWeave reached out to Texas's governor-elect regarding potential data center expansion opportunities in the state.

items.title: Berkshire Hathaway Ramps Up Buybacks in Post-Buffett Era
points: Berkshire spent $9.6 billion repurchasing shares in Q3 2026, more than double the $4.5 billion spent in Q2, bringing year-to-date buybacks to $14.4 billion through September.

This is a dramatic reversal from 2025, when Berkshire bought back zero shares, suggesting successor Greg Abel believes the stock trades below intrinsic value (a company's true underlying worth based on assets and earnings).
Berkshire's cash pile remains historic at $352 billion despite the buyback surge, leaving ample room for further repurchases or acquisitions.
Operating earnings fell 5.8% year-over-year to $12.7 billion, even as management signaled confidence in the business via buybacks.

items.title: Tech Stocks Trade Cheaper Than S&P 500 for First Time Since 2017
points: Technology stocks now trade at 17x forward earnings, below the S&P 500's 18x multiple — the first time tech has been cheaper than the broader index since 2017.
Wall Street is increasingly concerned about slower AI infrastructure spending growth following a massive capital deployment cycle.

items.title: AI Infrastructure vs. Big Tech: A Market Narrative Battle
points: Semiconductor/data-center stocks crashed post-election while Big Tech (Google, Microsoft, Amazon) stayed in the green, as a data center slowdown lowers chipmaker demand but cuts computing costs for hyperscalers.
Key earnings this week — CoreWeave (Tuesday), Nebius and Cerebras (Thursday) — will reveal whether the chip-sector slowdown is temporary or structural.
DataTrek's Nicholas Colas says the moves are AI-centric rather than recession signals, but traders must decide which narrative — infrastructure investment or Big Tech profit-taking — wins out.

items.title: Key Earnings and Economic Calendar This Week
points: Monday: Trump Media & Technology Group, Constellation Energy, and Occidental Petroleum report earnings.
Tuesday: CoreWeave earnings plus CPI inflation data could trigger repricing.
Thursday: Cisco, Applied Materials, Nebius, and Cerebras report.
Friday: PPI data and overnight earnings from Japanese banks Mitsubishi UFJ and Sumitomo Mitsui.

items.title: Oil Prices Fall as Trump Softens Tone on Iran
points: Oil prices dropped after Trump said extensive military strikes against Iran are "highly unlikely" if negotiations progress.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio countered that Tehran's current demands remain unacceptable, tempering the conciliatory signal.

items.title: Sports Betting's Hidden Toll: Problem Gamblers Drive Industry Revenue
points: More than half of American men aged 18-49 now bet on sports, per a three-year Bloomberg analysis of new bettors.
A small cohort (about 2.7% of bettors) showing signs of problem gambling generates roughly 60% of sportsbook revenue.
Studies from countries with longer legal online betting histories show problem gamblers face less retirement savings, greater isolation, higher unemployment, and increased mortality.

items.title: China's Shadow Debt Market Grows
points: Debt collectors in China are chasing as many as 100 million consumers struggling to repay loans.
The country's lack of a nationwide personal bankruptcy system is fueling a shadow market for bad debt.

items.title: U.S. Political Turbulence: Hegseth Impeachment Push and Deportation Rethink
points: House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries says he's a "hard yes" on impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over alleged abuse of power and national security threats.
Trump told CBS's 60 Minutes his administration may have been "too tough" on deportations and acknowledged the policy may have hurt Republicans in the midterms.

items.title: Retirement Savings Gaps Revealed by New Census Data
points: New Census data shows some retirees living on less than $2,000 per month.
Couples need between $800,000 and $1.33 million in retirement savings depending on their state of residence.
